plugins.name: designer
plugins.description: UI and UX for the crew: writes the design spec a developer builds and tests against (flow, every screen state, layout, copy, accessibility) and reviews existing UI for usability, WCAG 2.2 AA and consistency with the project's own tokens. Use when asked to design or spec a screen or flow, review UX or UI, check accessibility or contrast, or make an interface consistent.

plugins.name: developer
plugins.description: The development loop end to end, test-first: implement a feature in red-green-refactor slices, refactor without changing behaviour, diagnose a bug to its proved root cause, fix it with the failing test first, bisect a regression to the commit that caused it, run the repo's checks, then ship it as a ticket, branch and PR. Use when asked to implement, refactor, debug, fix a failing or flaky test, find what broke, or open a PR.

plugins.name: interview-prep
plugins.description: Prepares an engineer for one specific interview loop, not interviews in general. Maps the rounds a job description implies, ranks what to fix by risk, and runs graded mock rounds -- recruiter screen, live coding, take-home review, system design, behavioral, hiring manager -- against a rubric willing to say no. Keeps the STAR story bank and what real rounds asked. Use when preparing for an interview, practising answers, running a mock, building behavioral stories, or debriefing a round.

plugins.name: job-hunter
plugins.description: Runs a job or contract search as a pipeline. Searches Upwork, Arc and Contra against a declared profile, scores a posting as pursue or skip with the reason, writes portfolio case studies, tailors the application to one posting, and tracks follow-ups. Use when searching a platform for gigs, reviewing a job ad or RFP, deciding whether to bid, writing a proposal, cover letter or CV variant, or asking what needs chasing.

plugins.name: notes
plugins.description: Keeps running notes on many topics organized in plain Markdown: captures as you go, regroups each topic into In progress, TODO, Done and Notes without losing a line, shows what is open, and turns TODO, in-progress and inline "text"(todo|wip|done) markers into GitHub tickets, with "text"(outcome) as acceptance criteria, assigned to you on your default board or one named per item. Use when asked to note something, organize notes, list open TODOs, or file notes as tickets.

plugins.name: pair-programmer
plugins.description: Pairs on code instead of taking it over. Navigates while you drive -- holding the goal, questioning decisions before they are typed, catching a change spreading past its scope -- or plays TDD ping-pong where the suite decides when a turn ends. Keeps a journal of decisions, rejected alternatives and next steps, so work can be handed over. Use when the user wants to pair, asks for a second pair of eyes while coding, asks for ping-pong or test-first pairing, or asks whether a change is on track.

plugins.name: plugin-developer
plugins.description: Builds an agent plugin from a requirements prompt: splits it into testable requirements, maps each to the component that covers it (hooks, MCP servers and scripts only when needed), stops for approval, then scaffolds, tests and gates the plugin until it validates, loads and passes. Use when the user asks to build, plan or check a plugin or Claude Code extension from requirements.

plugins.name: prompt-engineer
plugins.description: Turns raw text — a task, rough notes, an example or an underperforming prompt — into a prompt tailored to the task, the target model and where it will live: a chat message, a system prompt, a pipeline template, an agent file or an image prompt. Asks only what it cannot work without, states every assumption, lints the result and tests it cold. Use when the user asks to write, improve or test a prompt, a system prompt or instructions for an LLM, agent or image model.

plugins.name: qa
plugins.description: Quality assurance for the crew: turns a ticket's acceptance criteria into a test plan before work starts, verifies the finished change against every criterion with evidence, on the ticket's review link if any, gives an accept or reject verdict and moves the ticket to Ready for Merge or back to In progress, and files reproducible bug tickets labelled "QA testing". Use when asked to test, QA or verify a change, check acceptance criteria, write test cases or a test plan, or report a bug.

plugins.name: recruiter-inbox
plugins.description: An actor agent for recruiter conversations on LinkedIn and email. Sweeps LinkedIn messages and InMails in your signed-in Chrome and recruiter email in Gmail, triages each one, drafts the reply that moves it toward a first call, and sends only the text you approved word for word; a hook stops anything else. Tracks who owes whom a reply. Use when answering recruiters, LinkedIn job offer messages, salary questions or follow-ups.

plugins.name: scrum-master
plugins.description: Backlog refinement and sprint planning against GitHub Issues. Turns raw requests into ready stories with acceptance criteria and a size, splits the ones that are too big, builds a sprint plan with one goal and a realistic capacity, and creates the GitHub Projects board the backlog goes on. Use when asked to refine or groom a backlog, write a user story, add acceptance criteria, estimate work, plan the next sprint, or create a project board.

plugins.name: skill-trainer
plugins.description: Keeps a senior engineer's skills sharp next to a full-time job: daily and weekly plans across coding, system design, stack deep-dives, practices and builds, honest grading and spaced review, plus an interview track for coding and system design. Stack, coding language and cadence are changeable settings. Use when asked for a study plan, today's practice, a coding drill, interview practice or progress.
